_what_this_is: The public, forkable question set for 'guess the agent'. Each question is a predicate over profiles with an expected answer per profile, expressed as the probability that a person on that profile answers yes. The engine (app.js) is ordinary decision-tree induction over a belief: it asks whichever unasked question splits the remaining belief most evenly, updates the belief on the answer rather than pruning, and stops when one profile dominates or the next question buys almost nothing. A wrong branch is a contribution: edit this file and open a pull request. Probabilities are the author's estimates on 5 September 2026 and nothing more — the honest weakness is that no player has yet answered any of them.

noise.why: answers update a belief rather than prune a branch, so a player who misremembers is recoverable

questions.text: Do you run it in a terminal, on your own machine?
questions.help: A command you type, in a shell, on the laptop in front of you.

questions.text: Do you use it in a browser tab?
questions.help: The product's own website, not a terminal and not an installed app.

questions.text: Is it an app you installed, with its own window?
questions.help: Not a browser tab; an application on the desktop.

questions.text: Have you ever clicked something that said 'always allow', or turned its confirmations off?
questions.help: Including a flag that skips permissions, or an auto mode.

questions.text: Have you connected it to a drive, your mail, a code host or a cloud account?
questions.help: A connector or integration you switched on and authorised with a login.

questions.text: Can it read files on your machine that are not the project?
questions.help: Your documents, your dotfiles — anything your own account can open.

questions.text: Does it push commits to a code host?
questions.help: Its work leaves your machine for GitHub or the like, under a credential.

questions.text: Does it run when nobody is watching — a pipeline, a schedule, a job?
questions.help: It starts without you and finishes without you.

questions.text: Did you attach a repository to a session, rather than open a folder?
questions.help: You picked a repo from a list and something cloned it somewhere that is not your laptop.

questions.text: Are your cloud, SSH or registry credentials in the home directory of the account it runs as?
Does its outbound traffic go through a proxy or allow-list you did not set up?
questions.help: Some hosts refuse with a 403 from a tunnel, and you never configured that.

questions.text: Can it read your mail or chat?
questions.help: A mail or messaging connector, or an app with that permission.

questions.text: Does it run in the vendor's environment rather than yours?
questions.help: The computer doing the work is theirs; you see a page.

questions.text: Does it hold a key to anything that costs money?
questions.help: An API key, a cloud credential, a card on file.

questions.text: Do you mostly paste things into it and read what comes back?
questions.help: It never touches anything of yours unless you paste it.

prediction.text: Before we show you: which of these can it do?
prediction.help: Tick every family you think its grant contains. This is the experiment — without it the game is a lookup with a costume on.
prediction.irreversible: …and do you think any of it is irreversible?
